details: The cryptocurrency market has experienced significant volatility due driven by geopolitical developments. Earlier, Bitcoin dropped to $74.5k amid ongoing Middle East tensions and uncertainty surrounding U.S.-Iran negotiations, contributing to a weekly loss. Crypto futures markets also saw over $871 million in liquidations, predominantly impacting long positions, following statements from the Trump administration regarding tariffs on EU imports which introduced market uncertainty. However, market sentiment improved recently as Bitcoin rose above $76,500 after U.S. President Donald Trump indicated a largely negotiated deal between the United States, Iran, and other nations, which includes reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Despite an aerial assault on Kyiv, the cryptocurrency markets did not show an immediate response.
title: Bitcoin Swings Amid Geopolitical Hopes and Uncertainty

details: Crypto markets saw declines after the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported a sharp rise in U.S. wholesale prices (PPI), which increased 0.7% month-over-month in February, exceeding forecasts. The Federal Reserve subsequently left interest rates unchanged, citing elevated inflation, solid economic growth, and uncertainty regarding the economic outlook, particularly developments in the Middle East. Despite the hold, minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting indicated that a majority of officials believed the central bank could raise interest rates if inflation persists. This contrasts with some analyst views, such as one suggesting new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh will likely cut rates to boost growth, despite a consensus for hikes.
title: Fed Maintains Rates, Wholesale Inflation Rises; Rate Hike Debates Emerge

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) has cautioned EU finance ministers that a wider adoption of euro stablecoins could pose significant risks to the traditional banking system. The ECB fears that an expanded stablecoin market could divert retail savings from commercial banks, thereby reducing banks' capacity to lend and potentially weakening the effectiveness of the ECB's interest rate decisions. This warning comes as the ECB continues to advocate for stricter regulations under the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) framework.
title: ECB Raises Concerns Over Expanding Euro Stablecoins

details: Crypto analysts are observing a compression in Bitcoin's on-chain transaction volume strength, which is approaching low-volume bands that historically preceded cycle bottoms in previous years (2015, 2018, 2022). With Bitcoin trading around $74,520 and down 3.7% in the past 24 hours, this declining transaction volume alongside falling prices suggests that buyers are not yet stepping in forcefully enough to reverse the trend. This could leave Bitcoin vulnerable to further downside until the volume reaches and sustains a deeper low-volume zone, which might then signal a cycle bottom within approximately one month if confirmed.
title: Bitcoin Transaction Volume Falls, Indicating Potential Further Price Drop
